transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Jonah Park (Redwood SE), Elena Torres (Omega CISO), Marcus Reed (Omega Head of Platform), Priya Banerjee (Compliance), David Hui (SRE)
Shared artifacts: Redwood SOC2 summary (link: drive/redwood/soc2-type2.pdf), draft SLA template (link: drive/redwood/sla-draft.xlsx), incident-playbook-template.docx

Auto-summary: Quick preface, then deep dive on incident notification chain, RTO/RPO examples, KMS BYOK options and audit log retention. Several clarifying questions on regulatory timelines and exec notification thresholds.

00:00 Samantha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate it. I'm Samantha from Redwood, i'm the account lead, with Jonah our solutions engineer. Quick audio check?
00:22 Elena (CISO): Hi, can you hear me, yes hi, audio is fine. We're mostly curious about your incident flow and how it meets our regulator requirements.
01:03 Jonah (Redwood SE): Great, thanks. I'll try to cover the technical trace — the runbook, our BCDR parameters (so RTO and RPO), and then we can go into SSO / RBAC, and KMS. Note there might be a bit of mess in transcription, apologies — somethings show up as sock two in the notes.
01:35 Marcus (Head of Platform): Yeah that's fine. We're particularly focused on two things: 1) Do you offer BYOK? 2) How fast can we get back to service for critical payment flows — what are typical RTO/RPO numbers?
02:10 Jonah: On BYOK — yes, customer-managed keys via KMS are supported. We typically integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS and HSM via a key wrapping layer. We call it KMS / bring-your-own-key. There's a rotation policy and we support key revoke patterns. For on-prem HSM we have a connector but that can affect recovery times.
02:48 Priya (Compliance): When you say rotation, does that mean you hold plaintext keys at any time? We need to avoid that for PCI regs.
03:12 Jonah: No, we never store plaintext keys. Keys are wrapped and only held in the cloud provider's KMS or customer HSM. There are short lived tokens, but we can provide architecture diagrams. We'll attach the KMS design doc.
03:42 Elena: Great. On logs — we need audit logs for 7 years and immutable export. How do you handle log retention and exports?
04:05 Samantha: By default we keep platform audit logs for 1 year for hosted customers, but for enterprise/private you can configure retention and export to your S3 or GCS bucket. We support an immutable export feed and signed log delivery. Typically we hand over a daily rolling export.
04:30 David (SRE): Can we request real-time streaming to our SIEM? We want near-zero delay for critical auth events.
04:49 Jonah: Yes, we support log streaming via Kafka or HTTPS webhooks — there's a ~10 to 30s latency under normal throughput for auth events. We'll include throughput caveats.
05:15 Marcus: Ok good. Let's talk RTO and RPO. What are your proven numbers?
05:35 Jonah: For hosted multitenant service our SLA is typically 99.9% by default, and we can move to 99.95% or 99.99% on Dedicated with reserved capacity. But RTO/RPO are more about the workload and what caches you're okay to lose. Example: for a stateless text gen path, common RTO is under 15 minutes for a failover to warm capacity; RPO is near-zero for request logs but session KV cache can be lost unless we persist it. If you need sub-5 minute RTO for payment-critical flow we recommend Dedicated with warm standby regions and persistent KV+disk replication.
06:40 Elena: Sub-5 min RTO sounds ideal for payments. What's the cost delta for warm standby?
06:55 Jonah: Approximately 1.6x to 2x the dedicated capacity cost depending on region and model. Also note that warm standby requires cross-region replication and config. We'll put a ballpark in the SLA draft.
07:20 Priya: For compliance, we need an incident timeline and exec escalation for PII exposures within 24 hours — how do you notify?
07:39 Samantha: We have layered notification: automated detection -> on-call pager (PagerDuty integration) -> incident commander -> exec alert if sev1/sev2 after 1 hour. We can customize the thresholds and include regulatory notification windows in contract.
08:15 Marcus: Who owns postmortem and what is the retention of evidence? Regulators will want chain of custody.
08:36 Jonah: Redwood owns the incident management for the platform layer; we produce the forensics packet and SHA-signed artifacts. We keep evidence per contract; we can provide chain-of-custody logs and we support export of the relevant artifacts so you can ingest them into your case management.
09:05 Elena: Good. Can you walk through an actual escalation flow — let's role-play a sev1 detection to exec?
09:28 Jonah: Sure. Detection -> automated alert into PagerDuty team A -> SRE triage within 5 minutes -> if not remediated, incident declared and incident commander (IC) assigned -> IC posts to incident channel and notifies on-call leads -> if customer-impacting and > 15 minutes, exec notifier goes out, legal and compliance looped in. We can change the thresholds.
10:02 David: On the on-call handoff, do you provide contact book and rotation schedule? Our SOC needs named contacts.
10:20 Samantha: We'll provide a named 24/7 on-call roster for your account for Dedicated customers, with escalation phone numbers and SSO-backed access for small-timeframes.
10:48 Marcus: About SLA credits — what is the credit formula?
11:05 Samantha: Standard credit: for monthly uptime below target you get pro-rated credit; e.g., for 99.95% threshold it's X% credit, for 99.9% Y% etc. We'll send a table in the SLA draft. Credits are applied to invoices, not cash refunds.
11:40 Elena: Speaking of uptime, what's your current platform SLA teleport — sorry typo — current uptime history?
11:55 Jonah: Our last 12 months for hosted API was 99.97% global, but that masks per-region blips. For Dedicated customers we have SLA-backed latency and uptime targets and run canary rollouts to avoid region-wide failures.
12:30 Marcus: Rolling upgrades are a big worry. Do you support automatic fallback to prior model versions if a canary fails?
12:50 Jonah: Yes, we have rollout policies with automatic fallback to a pinned version. Also we have traffic shaping by region and model compatibility routing.
13:25 Priya: For RBAC — how granular is your access control? We need fine grained roles for platform vs data access.
13:45 Jonah: RBAC supports org / project / route level permissions. You can assign roles like admin, dev, read-only, auditor. We also integrate with SCIM for provisioning through Okta. Sometimes the transcription writes SamL as Saml when the caps mis-read.
14:20 Elena: SSO flows — we want Just-in-time provisioning and enforced MFA for all accounts. Is that supported?
14:36 Samantha: Yes, we support SAML SSO with Just-in-time provisioning and enforced MFA. SCIM provides deprovisioning. We also offer session policies and conditional access if you want IP restrictions.
15:05 Marcus: How about audit log schema? We need immutable fields for actor, action, resource, timestamp, request-id.
15:25 Jonah: Our audit schema includes those fields and a request-id that ties to the token. We can stream logs in JSONL with signed timestamps; we also support CSV export if needed.
16:00 Priya: Retention for 7 years — you said default is 1 year. For compliance we need 7y, can that be contractual?
16:15 Samantha: Yes, for enterprise we can contract for 7-year retention and S3 lifecycle rules. There's cost implications — we'll include retention pricing in the cost addendum.
17:05 Elena: For incident response, can we run a tabletop with your team to simulate a PII leak on the inference path?
17:25 Samantha: Absolutely. We recommend a tabletop drill that covers detection to disclosure — detection, containment, forensics, customer notification, regulatory notification. We'll propose scenarios when we send dates.
18:00 Marcus: One more thing — data residency. Some EU accounts require data stay in EU. How granular is your routing?
18:20 Jonah: We can pin models and storage to regions; we support VPC + Private deployments for full data residency. For Hosted there are region pins and routing by policy. We'll list the region mapping in the private deployment spec.
19:00 Elena: Any notable compliance gaps? I assume SOC 2 is done, ISO in progress?
19:18 Samantha: We have SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 certification in progress with expected attestation by Q1 2026. We'll share current audit statements and the remediation backlog.
20:00 David: In case of catastrophic region failure, what's your BCDR plan? Warm standby, cold start, what are options?
20:24 Jonah: Options: 1) Cold start - cheapest, longer RTO (hours). 2) Warm standby - pre-warmed reserved capacity in another region with async replication (RTO tens of minutes). 3) Hot active-active - cross-region synchronized with near-zero RTO but higher cost. We recommend warm standby for most payment-critical paths.
21:10 Marcus: And RPO? For a stateful session store how are you doing replication?
21:30 Jonah: Session store replication depends on choice: persistent disk replication typically gives RPO in minutes; in-memory KV caches have higher RPO if not persisted. For sub-minute RPO you need synchronous replication with a hot-active design.
22:05 Elena: For the exec notification threshold, is there a way to auto-trigger legal and compliance emails with a template?
22:22 Samantha: Yes, incident commander can trigger an exec notification that includes templated fields and attachments (forensics packet attached). We can wire that to your legal distribution list.
23:00 Marcus: For onboarding, what's the timeline to get Dedicated with warm standby up and running?
23:20 Jonah: Typical onboarding 6-8 weeks for dedicated capacity and warm standby config, less if you're starting from hosted and small scope. There are infra approvals and network peering steps which can add time.
24:05 Priya: If we need SIEM integration, what's the authentication model for log streaming?
24:20 Jonah: We support mTLS for streaming endpoints, token-based auth and signed deliveries. We'll include example config for Splunk and Sumo in the follow-up.
25:00 Elena: Any previous incidents to share, redacted? We want to learn from your postmortems.
25:20 Samantha: We'll share anonymized postmortems and timelines; don't want to put PII in the transcript but we have two notable incidents last year — one was a region-level network flapping caused by a DB failover, the other was a regression in rollout that caused degraded latency. We'll include redacted summaries.
26:10 Marcus: For legal we need indemnities and data breach clauses — can we review sample contract language?
26:30 Samantha: Yes we'll provide sample language in the contract addendum. For financial services we typically add additional audit rights and periodic penetration testing schedules.
27:05 David: A small technical question — KV cache persistence and checkpointing, how often do you checkpoint?
27:20 Jonah: Default is periodic checkpoint every 5 minutes, configurable for Dedicated. Checkpoints are written to durable storage for the session store option.
28:00 Priya: For access controls, can we require just-in-time elevated privileges for incident investigations?
28:16 Jonah: Yes we support ephemeral elevations with approval flows through SSO/SCIM and we can log the approval chain in audit logs.
30:00 Samantha: Quick recap then we'll outline next steps. We will: 1) share SOC2 and ISO artifacts, 2) send draft SLA with tiers and credit table, 3) provide runbook mapping and PagerDuty example, 4) propose tabletop dates. Anything to add?
30:30 Elena: Please also include the KMS architecture and the BYOK connector docs.
31:02 Samantha: Noted. Jonah will own the KMS doc share.
31:20 Marcus: We'll assemble our RTO/RPO targets per service and send them back.
31:35 Elena: And we'd like a proof-of-concept for warm standby failover — is that possible?
31:48 Jonah: Yes, we can run a short PoC or failover drill in a sandbox for the critical flow. That would take ops time but is feasible.
32:10 Priya: For audit purposes, can we get signed time-stamped evidence of the drill?
32:25 Jonah: Yes, we can produce signed artifacts and logs for the drill and include a post-drill report.
33:00 Samantha: Alright, last few minutes for any detail.
33:12 Marcus: One thought — if we have dedicated on-prem connectors, how does software patching and scheduling work? We need maintenance windows.
33:32 Jonah: For Private deployments we coordinate maintenance windows with your SRE, apply patches in staging, then do canaries in production. We lock down automatic updates unless you opt-in.
34:05 Elena: Ok thanks. We'll expect the SOC2 and SLA draft this week.
34:18 Samantha: We'll aim to send docs by 2025-10-17 and schedule the tabletop the week of 2025-11-03.
35:00 David: One final question — do you support FIPS 140-2 HSM connectors?
35:18 Jonah: Yes, for enterprise we can integrate with FIPS certified HSMs; some vendors require contract addendums. We'll note that in the KMS doc.
36:00 (cross-talk, brief)
45:00 Samantha: Thanks all for the time. We'll follow up in writing with the artifacts listed.
58:00 Elena: Appreciate the thoroughness.
62:30 Samantha: Meeting end — we'll share the recording and notes. Thanks everyone.

Auto-generated action items (brief): Jonah to share KMS diagram and SOC2 link; Samantha to draft SLA; Omega to supply RTO/RPO per critical service.
